These findings suggest that Cytidine-5'-Monophosphate may act as a regulator or modulator of Thymidine kinase activity, possibly through the Cytidine-5'-Diphosphate intermediate. The evidence is consistent across two paths, with varying scores, but both highlight a shared pathway involving Cytidine-5'-Diphosphate as a critical mediator.
